customer: I've been trying to sell my leased pickup for two weeks and nobody can give me a straight answer on how it works. I run a small business out of Texas and I don't have time to keep chasing this. What do I actually need to do?
agent: Sorry for the runaround. Here's how it works: because a leased truck is owned by the leasing company, selling it to us is really a buyout from them, so first check that your leasing company allows third-party buyouts (see our article "Which leasing companies allow third-party buyouts"). If they do, you can ask them for a dealer payoff quote, which can be different from the payoff they quote to you, or you can sign the lease buyout authorization, form NW-LSE-1, and we'll request that dealer payoff quote for you. Bring the quote to your appointment, and if our offer comes in higher than the buyout, our article "If our offer is more than your lease buyout" explains what happens next.
